results.message: Explain identify the material with an example.
results.answer: To identify a material, examine what each part is actually made from rather than relying on its colour, appearance or pictures. Separate packages into their parts, then check the instructions for each part and your local collection service. For example, a snack package may have a cardboard sleeve and a soft-plastic wrapper: identify them separately because the sleeve’s recycling instructions may not apply to the wrapper. A scrunchable film is soft plastic, not a rigid container.

results.message: Explain connect waste and climate with an example.
results.answer:
Waste and climate are connected because producing food uses land, water and energy. When food is lost or wasted, those resources have been used without providing nutrition, and the discarded food can contribute to greenhouse-gas emissions. Globally, food loss and waste together are linked to about 8–10% of annual greenhouse-gas emissions. This supports SDG 13.3, which includes climate education and awareness.

Example: Plan meals and store food properly so edible vegetables are used instead of thrown away. Unavoidable scraps can go through an accepted organics collection service, but this does not undo the resources already used to produce them.

results.message: 请简单解释联系浪费与气候。
results.answer:
食物浪费与气候有关，因为食物在生产、运输和储存前后都需要土地、水和能源；食物被浪费时，这些投入也随之被浪费。全球年度温室气体排放中，约有 8%–10% 与食物损失和浪费有关，这一数据合并计算了“损失”和“浪费”，不是个人已经节省的排放量。

日常例子：先按需要购买和烹调食物，妥善保存剩余食物，能减少可避免的浪费。无法避免的食物残余可按当地规定进行有机物收集，但这不能抵消食物生产时已经使用的资源。

results.message: 请简单解释逐个阅读部件。
results.answer:
逐个阅读部件，就是不要把整个包装当成一个整体处理：

1. 先找出每个部件，例如盒子、内膜和盖子。
2. 分别阅读每个部件旁边的处理标识或说明。
3. 判断它是可回收、有条件可回收，还是不可回收；有条件时要遵守准备步骤或指定收集方式。
4. 只按说明要求分离部件，不要把一个部件的标识套用到整个包装上。

例如，吃完盒中食物并安全清除残余后，分别查看盒身和盖子的说明。玻璃罐盖的处理规则可能因当地 council 而不同，因此不能一概而论。

results.message: Explain prepare accepted recycling with an example.
results.answer: Prepare items according to the receiving service’s rules, because acceptance is not universal. Empty accepted containers and rinse them if needed; keep accepted mixed-recycling items loose when required; keep paper and cardboard clean and dry; and remove packaging and fruit stickers from FOGO scraps. If you cannot confirm acceptance, check first rather than adding it. Example: separate a yogurt tub from a banana peel—place the tub in its accepted recycling stream only if the service takes it, and put the peel in the accepted organics/FOGO stream without packaging or stickers. Local collection rules vary, so check your service’s guidance.

results.message: Explain reuse suitable items with an example.
results.answer:
Reuse means keeping a suitable item in use instead of replacing it after one use. For example, use a reusable water bottle, cup or shopping bag repeatedly. Check that it is suitable, clean it, and follow its care instructions. Do not repurpose packaging in ways that could create food or chemical safety risks. Recycling also requires collection and processing, so safe reuse can be considered first.

Example: carry a clean, reusable shopping bag on future trips instead of taking a new disposable bag each time.

results.message: Explain plan with available food with an example.
results.answer:
Before shopping, check your fridge, freezer and pantry. Choose food that needs using soon while it is still safe, plan a meal around it, and add only missing ingredients to your list. Check portions and plan for the people who will eat.

Example: If you have carrots and half a tub of another ingredient, plan a meal using them before choosing a recipe that requires a new shop. If your plans change, review the perishables and make a safe storage plan.

results.message: Explain put safety first with an example.
results.answer:
Put safety first by following the food’s storage instructions and treating a use-by date as a safety limit. Keep perishable food refrigerated at 5°C or colder, and do not eat it after its use-by date. A best-before date mainly concerns quality, but the food still needs to have been stored properly.

Example: Keep cooked leftovers in the fridge, label them with the date, and use them before the relevant safety limit. If they are past the use-by date, discard them rather than relying on smell or reheating.

results.answer: “安全优先”是指先确认食物仍在安全期限内，并遵守标签上的储存要求，再考虑如何减少浪费。标有 use-by 的食物超过日期不要食用；best-before 主要关系品质，但仍要检查储存条件和食物状态。不要只靠气味判断，也不能自行延长 use-by 日期。比如：把易腐食物冷藏在 5°C 或以下，并在 use-by 日期前安排使用。

results.message: Explain prevent surplus first with an example.
results.answer: “Prevent surplus first” means avoiding buying or preparing more food than people are likely to use. Before shopping, check your fridge, freezer and pantry; plan around ingredients that need using soon, estimate portions, and buy only what is missing. For example, if you already have carrots and half a tub of another ingredient, plan a meal using them instead of buying ingredients for a completely new recipe. If plans change, review perishables and store them safely.

results.message: 请简单解释先预防多余食物。
results.answer:
先预防多余食物，就是在购物前先查看冰箱、冷冻室和储物柜，优先安排仍安全、需要尽快使用的食物；再根据实际人数和份量购物，只购买缺少的东西。这样可以减少买多、忘记使用和最后变质的情况，也能避免白白浪费食物生产所需的土地、水和能源。

例子：家里已有胡萝卜和半盒食材，就先围绕它们计划一餐，再把缺少的食材列入购物清单。

results.message: Explain read dates and scope with an example.
results.answer:
Read the publication date separately from the review date. A publication date tells you when the source was issued; a review date tells you when the supplied material was checked. If no publication date is provided, it should not be treated as the review date. Also check the scope: “global” applies worldwide, while “AU-VIC” applies to Victoria, Australia, and should not automatically be assumed to apply to another council or region.

Example: the UNFCCC source was published on 30 September 2024, reviewed on 5 October 2026, and has global scope. Its 8–10% figure refers to combined food loss and food waste worldwide—not emissions saved by an individual learner. A Victorian waste-sorting page has no stated publication date, is regional to Victoria, and was reviewed on 5 October 2026.

results.message: 请简单解释阅读年份与范围。
results.answer: “阅读年份”要区分两种时间：统计年份是数据实际观察或测量的年份；报告年份是报告发布的年份。例如，这份食物浪费估计的统计年份是 2022 年，报告发布于 2024 年，不能把它当作对你今天厨房的测量。阅读范围也要看清：数据可能是全球范围，并且“食物损失和浪费”是合并计算的；8%–10%指全球年度温室气体排放的相关比例，不是个人节省的排放量。分享数据时，最好同时注明年份、单位和范围。
